rule: The film's voice-over, word for word: the ElevenLabs narration mixed onto the cut after the render (README.md, 'On the landing'). film/vtt.mjs writes the landing's captions track from it. Each line names the shot it is spoken over, as beat id/slot id of lib/beats.mjs; each cue's from and to are seconds from that shot's start: from the first to the last sound of the line in the mix, held 0.3 s longer (never past the shot's end), and a long line of two sentences splits at the pause between them. A line moves with its shot, so a new shot list needs new times here and a new mix.

cues.text: Over a weekend, the feed is held for days without an update.
So the vault keeps the exchange's hours.
Maat's agent runs on Claude, and only proposes.
On Basescan, a refusal reads Success.
This is the owner's own treasury, and the vault holds its limits: per trade, per day, per stock.
Change one word of the rationale, and the hash stops matching.
You need not take our word for it.
The exchange was shut for Thanksgiving.
On a market holiday, the vault refuses every trade.
Two probes asked the vault that day: allowed before the close, refused after.
A brief is a short public message on Base.
The vault cannot: whatever a brief talks it into is weighed by the same rules.
Each address is public. Read it yourself.
The tests run in the open.
